reasons: The cited Section 10(a) is a genuine Vendor-side defend/indemnify/hold-harmless obligation running to Customer and its personnel for all third-party Claims (including reasonable attorneys' fees) arising out of the Services, Auction Platform, Creative, Kubient's breach of warranty, and Kubient's acts/omissions — subject-matter triggers broad enough to capture third-party IP infringement/misappropriation allegations relating to the Services or Platform, so the rule's core requirement is satisfied.

The failed deterministic check is a phrasing artefact: the clause never uses 'infringe' or 'intellectual property', but the substantive scope required by the rule (and more) is present; the rationale correctly identifies and explains this.

The clause exceeds the fallback: no Customer-modification/combination/specification carve-outs, no procure/modify/replace/refund sole-remedy cap, no 3x super-cap, and Section 7(a) expressly excludes indemnification from the consequential-damages waiver. Section 11 supplies the preferred procedure (prompt notice with no forfeiture for delay, indemnitor control, no liability-admitting settlement without consent, cooperation at indemnitor's cost).

The two shortfalls flagged (broader reciprocal Customer indemnity in 10(b) and the 'to the best of its knowledge' qualifier on the Creative limb) are correctly treated as minor sub-preferred points noted in the rationale rather than redlined, consistent with the playbook's classification semantics; the clause on balance benefits our party.
Consistent with a compliant finding, no redline text was altered and no counterparty comment was proposed — appropriate for retention as internal evidence rather than a negotiation issue.
